Every node has exactly d neighbors; d=2 is a single cycle visiting the nodes in random order. The graph is only likely to be a good expander and is not checked, which is what the maybe means." width="100%"} Creates `n` nodes and lays `d / 2` random cycles through all of them, each one drawn again (up to `max_tries` times) until it shares no edge with the cycles before it. The union is a simple, connected `d`-regular graph. Friedman's theorem says such a graph is almost always nearly Ramanujan, with second-largest adjacency eigenvalue close to the optimal `2 sqrt(d - 1)`, but this method doesn't check; `add_random_regular_expander_graph()` retries until the bound holds, and `is_regular_expander()` checks a graph. It is NetworkX's `maybe_regular_expander()`. A random cycle avoids the `k - 1` cycles before it with probability only about `exp(-2 (k - 1))`, so the default `max_tries=100` is plenty for `d` up to `6` but should be raised for larger degrees (to about `20 * exp(d - 2)`). In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Unions of random cycles are useful for: - quickly generating sparse, well-connected regular graphs of any even degree - random expanders for testing network robustness, mixing and load balancing - Hamiltonian test graphs (every one contains a Hamiltonian cycle by construction) ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. Must be positive and at least `d + 1`. [d]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Degree of every node: an even number, at least `2`. [max_tries]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : How many times each cycle may be redrawn before giving up. Default is `100`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is not positive, `d=` is odd or less than `2`, `n - 1` is less than `d=`, or a cycle disjoint from the others isn't found in `max_tries=` draws. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A 4-regular graph on 50 nodes, from two disjoint Hamiltonian cycles: ::: {#e34447bb .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_maybe_regular_expander(n=50, d=4, seed=1) graph.count_edges(), set(graph.degrees(return_dict=True).values()), graph.is_simple() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (100, {4}, True) ``` ::: ::: It is (almost always) an expander: ::: {#4b7359b1 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.is_regular_expander() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: :::
